Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday — the team and I are working through the pilot economics and ran into a couple of concrete questions the finance folks asked me to confirm before we move to PO. Can you confirm the following?

1) Trigger for min-charge: If a request is very short (e.g., 6 tokens) but we hit a heartbeat/keepalive on a connection that keeps KV warm, does Redwood bill the min-charge for the whole session bucket or just the 6 tokens for that call?

2) Fractional tokens: We saw small fractional token lines on our preview invoice. Are fractions always rounded up per-call, aggregated across a rolling window, or do you use some form of smoothing?

3) Long context streams: For streaming calls where we keep appending context over a user session (30+ prompts, sometimes hitting 20k history), how do you attribute token usage if we pin a model version vs. switching to an online compressed model mid-session? Any re-attribution rules we should be aware of?

4) Prefix reuse and credits: If we have a large static system prompt we reuse across users, does Redwood credit prefix reuse or is that always charged as new tokens per call?

I've attached a small sample invoice excerpt so you can see the rows our CFO is flagging. Appreciate a short written explanation we can send upstream. If easier, a quick 30m to walk through would also work.

Subject: Re: Questions on min charge triggers and fractional rounding — technical details and examples

Hi Anna, Sergio — sorry for the longer reply, wanted to include precise rules and two short examples based on CloudCorp's sample rows. Attaching a one-page PDF and an Excel with worked math.

Summary answers (short):
1) Min-charge/trigger behavior: Redwood bills per-request usage by default. There is an additional active-session minimum that applies when a customer has an open reserved session (e.g., dedicated pools or long lived private sessions) — that is only applied when the session is pinned to a reserved compute bucket. For hosted API calls, a single short call that does not maintain a reserved session will be billed by per-token usage (no session min).

2) Fractional tokens & rounding: We do metering at the token-precision level and keep a rolling aggregation window (1 hour) for smoothing. Fractions from multiple calls in that window are summed and rounded at the window boundary. So small fractional lines on previews typically represent interim windows and will reconcile on invoice to the rounded value. We only round upward on the invoice level when the aggregated fraction exceeds the billing quantum; otherwise it's zeroed. See Example A below.

3) Long context / model switching: Token attribution is tied to the request that caused the tokens to be emitted. If you switch models mid-session, tokens produced after the switch are attributed to the new model SKU. For KV/prefix caching, if a pinned session keeps the KV warm and you later switch to a compressed variant, KV reuse credits will only apply when the runtime identifies identical key prefixes across requests and the session type supports prefix-crediting (private and dedicated have stronger crediting guarantees than hosted).

4) Prefix reuse credits: We offer prefix reuse crediting for static system prompts when they match exactly and the request pattern reuses cached KV entries. For hosted API customers, prefix reuse is provided opportunistically (depends on routing and batching) — credits are best-effort. For Dedicated/Private customers, we can enable deterministic prefix-crediting and reflect it as a line-item credit on the invoice.

Example A — fractional rounding (simplified):
- Calls in hour window: 0.4 token, 0.3 token, 0.5 token (aggregated fractional = 1.2 tokens)
- Billing quantum = 1 token => invoice will show 1 token billed for that window; leftover 0.2 may be carried forward per your contract (we can waive carry-forwards for pilots).

Example B — short call + heartbeat: (hosted API)
- Single short call 6 tokens, connection idle afterwards — billed as 6 tokens. No session minimum applied.
- If same pattern runs against a Dedicated reserved session (session pinned) and policy is configured with a session floor of 50 tokens per minute, the floor would apply while the session is active.

Attached: unitization_summary.pdf and redwood_calc_examples.xlsx with row-by-row mapping for your sample invoice. Happy to simulate CloudCorp's month if you send a larger CSV.
